calls.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept.
Create ONE original visual candidate board for the luggage-organizing tutorial of the game "Next Stop, Russia!". This is an unapproved TEMP art and interaction concept, NOT a running game screenshot or final design.
Show two clearly separated screen-composition mockups on a neutral presentation board: a large landscape PC view at 16:9 and a smaller portrait phone view at about 360:780. Make these actual visual game interfaces, not prose diagrams.
In each interface, exactly FOUR easily recognizable illustrated objects: a thick textbook taking TWO cell units, a plain passport booklet without national seal or personal information taking ONE unit, a folded scarf ONE unit, and a small zipped toiletry washbag ONE unit. Their soft rounded shapes, subtle ink outlines and simple flat shading must be a single consistent original visual family, readable at small size.
Exactly THREE open storage compartments A, B, C: A visibly divided into two unit spaces, B two unit spaces, C one unit space. Capacity should be understandable from actual slot outlines and object footprints, not just colored categories. Arrange the PC view with unpacked items at left, large storage areas center/right, actions at bottom. Phone view has storage areas above an unpacked-items tray, a fixed bottom action row, large touch targets and generous gaps. Show a subtle dragged textbook and destination ghost outline in PC; phone shows an item selected with a large target highlight. Do not imply a new puzzle rule or unique-answer comparison.
Temporary aesthetic candidate only: clear, gentle, uncluttered, modest warm accents, high contrast object silhouettes. Show only minimal glyph text A B C, with blank title and instruction areas for future engine-rendered Russian and Chinese.
Place legible board header EXACTLY "CANDIDATE / TEMP_REPLACE_REQUIRED". No approval stamp, no currency, timers, stars, shop, gameplay code, existing franchise or Kenney assets. Do not copy any reference artwork.
calls.review: Rejected for unrelated train/Moscow-like scenery; retained only in built-in output directory.

1) Arrival in Saint Petersburg, first-person student viewpoint with a plain suitcase, broad quiet river embankment, restrained low-rise northern European classical facades, overcast sky. Generic place impression, no claim of accurate street geography. Absolutely no Moscow Kremlin or Saint Basil cathedral, no copied landmarks or real photos.
2) Friendly adult woman Anna, temporary waist-up character concept, speaking in that arrival environment. No other invented NPC.
3) Older female dormitory administrator behind a simple reception desk handing over one plain room key, in a readable dorm lobby environment; show a small open doorway suggesting the transition into the room.

calls.review: CANDIDATE; three Q00 story moments plus portrait study. Characters and geography not approved.

calls.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / ui-mockup. Create ONE entirely original unapproved dorm-room visual candidate board for "Next Stop, Russia!". Header exactly "CANDIDATE / TEMP_REPLACE_REQUIRED".
Main composition: a wide comfortable student dormitory interior viewed BASICALLY FRONTALLY into the room, with only a mildly elevated viewpoint that reveals the bed top, desk top, floor and some furniture sides. Not orthographic overhead, not isometric, no complete ceiling required. It should feel inhabited and layered without copying any existing game artwork: stable bed on left, writing desk around center with window behind, wardrobe on right, small suitcase and rug in the foreground. Furnishings at different depths, generous visible floor, a readable foreground/midground/background. These placements are only an illustrative provisional composition, not new committed game coordinates.
A temporary fluffy gray cat peeks partly out beside or under a piece of furniture, clearly discoverable, do not cover its eyes/head with interface.
Small, subtle furniture vocabulary plaques must appear ON the furniture surfaces, not uniformly floating above: exact words "кровать" on bed footboard/front rail; "стол" on desk front apron; "шкаф" on wardrobe door; "окно" on lower window frame, avoiding the cat. Keep plaques large enough to be legible, but do not pretend these baked concept labels are production UI.
Include a smaller portrait phone composition study alongside, about 360:780, showing a LARGE readable slice of this SAME near-frontal room with horizontal browsing implied by quiet left/right arrows. The portrait must use its own UI arrangement, not squash the wide scene to fit; optional narrow life-activity sidebar and a bottom row of large touch controls. Keep label separation readable.
Art treatment: a coherent modestly outlined illustrative candidate, calm lighting, restrained texture and warm accents; no named artist style, no specific copied reference furniture/people/decor, no official visual approval, no full 3D scene, no player avatar walking, coins, scores, level maps or extra pet systems. Do not include text other than the header and the four short Russian vocabulary words.
calls.review: Rejected for unrequested exterior landmarks/posters; retained only in built-in output directory.
